verdict.rationale: First-party docs state that Next.js apps can be self-hosted on a Node.js server, as a Docker image, or as static HTML exports, so the core self-hosting capability is documented. Community reports describe friction and claim some features work only on Vercel, but no one reports that self-hosting fails outright. missing for 10: in-depth evidence of feature parity when self-hosted, independent hands-on corroboration of smooth Node/Docker deployments.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Learn how to self-host your Next.js application on a Node.js server, Docker image, or static HTML files (static exports).
Next.js enables starting as a static site or Single-Page Application (SPA), then later optionally upgrading to use features that require a server.
